Per client means per API key where there is one and per source address where there isn't. Don't invent a third case.
turns.reply:
Found the middleware stack. `RequestScopeMiddleware` already resolves the client identity, so the limiter hooks in directly after it and gets the key for free.

class RateLimiter:
    pass

turns.prompt: Use a per-client token bucket, not a fixed window — bursts should smooth out.
turns.reply:
Swapped the stub for a token bucket keyed by client id: 100 tokens, refilled continuously over 60 seconds, so a client that has been quiet can spend a burst and one that is saturated is smoothed rather than cut off at a window boundary.

The bucket state is in-process. That is correct for one gateway and wrong for three behind a load balancer, which is a decision for you rather than for me.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.input:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/app/http/rate_limit.py
@@
-class RateLimiter:
-    pass
+class TokenBucketLimiter:
+    def __init__(self, rate: int = 100, per_seconds: int = 60) -> None:
+        self.rate = rate
+        self.per_seconds = per_seconds
+        self._buckets: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
+
+    def allow(self, client: str, now: float) -> bool:
+        tokens, last = self._buckets.get(client, (self.rate, now))
+        tokens = min(self.rate, tokens + (now - last) * self.rate / self.per_seconds)
+        if tokens < 1:
+            self._buckets[client] = (tokens, now)
+            return False
+        self._buckets[client] = (tokens - 1, now)
+        return True
*** End Patch

workspaces.description: Moving auth token resolution off the cookie jar and onto the request scope, with the legacy header path kept behind a flag.

tickets.title: Auth token reads from the cookie jar on every request
Legacy header auth path has no deprecation plan
Auth guide still documents the cookie-jar read

Move auth to request-scope tokens

phase.note: Re-running the auth suite before wrap-up

tickets.note: PR is up, waiting on review

Blocked on a decision: pin the fallback, or delete it

turns.prompt:
We read the session token out of the cookie jar on every request, and it shows up in three different places with three different fallbacks.

Move token reading off the cookie jar and onto the request scope. Resolve it once per request, hang it on the request object, and have everything downstream read that.

Start by showing me what's actually there — I don't want a rewrite of code neither of us has looked at.
turns.reply:
Token resolution happens in `RequestScopeMiddleware._read_token`, and it is already once per request — the problem is that nothing downstream trusts that, so two other call sites re-read the cookie themselves.

Three things stand out:
  1. The middleware writes `request.state.token`, so the request-scope slot already exists and is already populated.
  2. `context.read_token_from_cookie` re-reads the jar and re-parses, which is where the second and third fallbacks live.
  3. The legacy `X-Auth-Token` header path is checked only in the second reader, so the two disagree about what an authenticated request is.

So this is less a move than a deletion: the destination already works. What I do not yet know is who depends on the legacy header, and I would rather find that out before changing a signature.
